issue.title: Independently check the second zero of S1 near omega/omega_inf 1.0989 with another summation
issue.body:
**What.** An independent check of the second zero of S₁ (#82): a fresh agent, given only the σ data (raw I82-win2's three K 45 J 1500 JSONs, `sigma_str`) and the statement, locates the zero x₁ of S₁ near x = A² ≈ 13.5 at ω/ω∞ = 1.09, 1.10 and 1.11. It uses a summation method of its own, not Borel–Padé: for example a conformal map of the Borel plane with Padé, Hermite–Padé, or direct high-order analytic continuation. Then it finds where Im x₁ changes sign.

**Why.** #82's K 45 test puts the crossing at ω/ω∞ = 1.0988–1.0989 in every ring-free Borel–Padé sum, with both planted controls passing (notes/HARMONY.md). That is a second selected solution of the D = ∞ inner problem, with Δ ≈ 1.496. A result of this weight needs a second method sharing nothing but the coefficients (AGENTS.md).

**Acceptance (can fail).**
- The checker's own method finds a sign change of Im x₁ between 1.09 and 1.11, or it doesn't. Its crossing is compared with 1.0989.
- Planted truth through the same code: a crossing planted at 1.095 is found within 0.005, and one at 1.15 is rejected.
- The shared inputs are recorded.

**Depends on.** #82.

comments.body: started: independent checker (coordinator's subagent) on the Apple M5 Mac (`mac`), worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-a0b46a8c83bdfc168` of nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d at 442018c, one process under `nice -n 10`. Code under `solver/independent_second_zero/`, backed up to `wip/i203`; logs in raw folder `I203-mac/`. Method: not Borel–Padé (named in the plan posted before the real-data run).

Progress (mac, 2026-11-08 23:30 UTC, one process, cpu ~1 thread of 10, memory < 0.3 GB).

The planted-truth criteria are in the raw README, committed before any zero of S1 was computed from the real data: `I203-mac/README.md` at raw commit 0db9587.

Method, not Borel–Padé. The ratios σ_{n−1}/σ_n grow linearly in n, so S1(x) is entire of exponential type and F(t) = Σ n! σ_n t^n (its Laplace transform at 1/t) has a finite radius. F is continued by quadratic Hermite–Padé approximants (P F² + Q F + R = O(t^{p+q+r+2}), primary) and by linear Padé of F in t (cross-check). The approximant's own Taylor coefficients replace the missing c_n, S1 is summed term by term as Σ c̃_n x^n/n!, and x1 follows by Newton on that series. Both transforms multiply by n!, the opposite of Borel.

The planted family is e^{za x} [1F1(a+da; b; (zp−za) x) + 0.05 1F1(a+da+1; b+3/2; (zp−za) x)]. Its (za, zp, a, b)(w) come from a Kummer fit to the data's σ_1..σ_22, which matches each coefficient to 0.2–0.9%, so it has the data's one-cut structure. The constant da puts the zero at 13.5 exactly at w_p. A development run (w_p 1.105, seed 99, not one of the controls) is going now, then the controls P1 and P2, then the real data.

Code: `solver/independent_second_zero/` at `wip/i203` 66748aa.

Progress (mac, 2026-11-08 23:42 UTC, one process under `nice -n 10`, ~1 of 10 cores, memory < 0.3 GB).

**Control failure in estimator v1.** v1 used only the qhp approximants built from all 23 coefficients as its primary set. It failed P1 and P2 at seed 3. At w = 1.11 (noise seed 2003), the 1e-12 noise gave every 23-coefficient qhp approximant a far singularity, with growth 2.7–6.3 against the admission bound 2.3, so the primary set was empty at that node. Seeds 1, 2, 4 and 5 passed both controls, and their P1 crossings were 1.09500 ± 1e-5. v1 never ran on the real data, because I stopped its script before that step.

**Estimator v2** (code 3af9d9b) pools the qhp sets built from 21, 22 and 23 coefficients. The admission rules and the README criteria are unchanged. Seeds 1–5 are the controls. Seeds 6–10 are extra and have not been run before. The v2 run is going now, P1 and P2 first, then the real data, then a stress family with eps 0.3 that is information only.

Raw: `I203-mac/` at raw commit 890e18d (`v1/` holds the failed controls). Code: `wip/i203` 3af9d9b.

**Closing summary (independent checker, mac, 2026-11-09 00:41 UTC).** My method finds a sign change of Im x1 between 1.09 and 1.11. The crossing is at **w = 1.09884** (envelope 1.09873–1.09894), against the claimed 1.0988–1.0989. At 1.10 it gives **x1 = 13.46562 − 0.01372i**, against the claimed 13.465 − 0.013i. Both controls pass under estimator v2 after v1 failed them, details below.

**Method.** Laplace-plane continuation, not Borel–Padé. The ratios σ_{n−1}/σ_n grow linearly in n, so S1 is entire of exponential type, and F(t) = Σ n! σ_n t^n has a finite radius. F is continued by quadratic Hermite–Padé approximants, P F² + Q F + R = O(t^{p+q+r+2}) with degrees 5–9 (Shafer 1974). This is the primary method, and it uses 21, 22 or 23 coefficients, pooled. Linear Padé of F in t is the cross-check. The approximant's Taylor coefficients give S̃(x) = Σ_{n≤220} c̃_n x^n/n!, and x1 is the Newton zero of that series from 13.5. Fixed rules (`lapl.admissible`) reject an approximant that is degenerate, or that has a singularity well inside the data's disc (growth > 1.25 |ζ_DS|) or a tail of more than 30 times the largest data term at |x| = 13.5. The method assumes that the approximant's singularities near the true ones are what fix S at |x| ≈ 13.5, and that the coefficients past n = 22 are the approximant's.

**Per node** (primary set: 52 qhp approximants, all admitted at all three nodes):

| w | x1 | ± |
|---|---|---|
| 1.09 | 13.40094 + 0.10383i | 7.8e-4, 1.3e-3 i |
| 1.10 | 13.46562 − 0.01372i | 7.4e-4, 1.1e-3 i |
| 1.11 | 13.52899 − 0.13216i | 6.9e-4, 1.0e-3 i |

Each ± is half the range over approximant choices (degree triples and numbers of coefficients). It is a spread, not an error bound.

**Crossing.** The quadratic through the three medians gives 1.09884. Its envelope over the ±spread is 1.09873–1.09894, and all 52 approximants' own crossings lie in 1.09875–1.09894. By number of coefficients, the qhp sets give 1.09884 (23), 1.09884 (22) and 1.09880 (21). The linear Padé cross-check gives 1.09894, envelope 1.09863–1.09923.

**Controls.** The criteria were committed before any real-data zero, at raw 0db9587.

| control | verdict |
|---|---|
| v1 (primary = 23-coefficient qhp only), P1 and P2 | **FAIL at seed 3**: at w = 1.11 the 1e-12 noise gave every 23-coefficient qhp approximant a far singularity, so the primary set was empty there. v1 never ran on the real data. |
| v2 (pools 21–23; rules and criteria unchanged), P1 at 1.095 | pass, seeds 1–5 and extra seeds 6–10. Crossings 1.09499–1.09500, so the error is ≤ 8e-6. |
| v2, P2 at 1.15 | pass, 10/10 seeds. Im x1 is +0.436, +0.361, +0.286, matching the truth to 1e-4, with no sign change. |
| mutation: partial sum only | fires. Zeros come out near 8.5 − 0.6i, with no crossing. |
| stress, eps 0.3 (information only) | crossing error ≤ 5e-6 |

The planted family is e^{za x}[1F1(a+da; b; Δx) + eps 1F1(a+da+1; b+3/2; Δx)], with its parameters from a Kummer fit to the data. That fit matches each σ_n to 0.2–0.9%.

**Caveats.**
- The real data's per-node spread (1e-3) is about 20× the planted one (5e-5), so the planted family is easier than the data. Its accuracy is not an error bar for the real result.
- The crossing needs σ_n to about 1e-10 relative. Adding 1e-9 noise widens the envelope to 1.0934–1.1005, and 1e-6 moves the crossing to 1.1008. The fit plateaus put the σ_n at ≤ 1.3e-14, but that is the same fit's own estimate.

**Read:**
- AGENTS.md and the issue body.
- The `amp_flint_par.py` docstring (lines 1–43) and its output section (lines 600–690). They confirm σ_n = S_1^(2n+1)/S_1^(1), the order-ε^{2n+1} coefficient of the harmonic-1 multiplier, so S1 ∝ Σ σ_n x^n with x = ε². Identifying ε² with A² is the issue's statement.
- The three JSONs: `sigma_str`, plus `fit_info` and `sigma_err` for the error estimate.
- The "k 1/3/43/45" lines of `I82-win2/w1.0x.log`, for |S_1^(1)|.

**Not read:** `second_zero_nodes.py`, `zerolib.py`, `plant_x1.py`, notes/HARMONY.md, #82's comments, `I82-win2/README.md`.

**Shared with the original:** the σ coefficients and their generator, the representation in x, the node set, the start x = 13.5, and mpmath.

**Raw:** `I203-mac/`, results at 75e44bc and sensitivity at a74bf45 (head a74bf45). **Code:** `wip/i203` 43a353e, `solver/independent_second_zero/`.

**Discrepancies:** none with the claimed crossing or x1. One reported finding: `sigma_err` in the three JSONs is DBL_MAX for every σ_n, because the k = 1 fit has err inf, so the JSON's own error field is unusable. AGENTS.md says to check it.

**Recommended tasks**
1. *A planted family with a non-hypergeometric discontinuity for the second-zero estimators.* What: build a family whose Laplace-conjugate discontinuity is not of Beta/Kummer form, fitted to the data's σ to better than 0.1%, and run `second_zero.py planted` on it. Why: on the real data the approximants spread 20× more than on the present planted family. Acceptance: the crossing at a planted 1.095 is found within 0.005 and the planted x1 lies within 3× the reported spread, or the spread is shown to underestimate the error. Depends on #203.
2. *The J-stability of σ_18–σ_22 at 1e-10, if #82 does not already show it.* What: compare σ at J 1200 and 1500 (K 45, 1.10). Why: the crossing needs σ_n to about 1e-10 relative, and the plateau estimate (≤ 1.3e-14) comes from the same fit. Acceptance: max relative difference over n ≤ 22 is below 1e-10, or the crossing is rerun with the difference as noise. Depends on #82.
3. *Make `sigma_err` usable.* What: `amp_flint_par.py` takes e1 = S1_err[1] = inf, which makes every `sigma_err` DBL_MAX. Use 0 or the k = 1 plateau. Acceptance: `sigma_err` is finite and matches `coef_err.py`'s estimate to a factor of 2. Depends on nothing.

Coordinator review. I reran `second_zero.py real` on I82-win2 (exit 0). Every approximant family crosses at 1.0988–1.0991, as reported. Merged as c7f6f77, with notes/HARMONY.md's paragraph in 4acb009. Verdict: confirmed by a second method. The crossing is at 1.09884 against Borel–Padé's 1.0988–1.0989, and x₁ agrees to 1e-3. v1's estimator failed its planted controls before it touched the real data. v2 changed only the pooling of approximant orders, not a threshold, and passes on ten seeds. The recommended tasks are #213 (σ against J), #214 (a non-Kummer planted family), and #199 for `sigma_err`.
